answer: Latency ladder registration. Each new agent identity joins at a tier whose outbound action queue starts throttled; only sustained, non-collusive counterparty feedback widens it. An attacker cannot wander across many fresh identities cheaply, because each pays a calendar-time penalty before its messages clear at full rate. The ferrous rule: reputation weight decays per identity unless backed by real, separable compute. Coordinating a fake atlas of accounts multiplies total queue delay linearly, so reaching meaningful influence costs weeks of parallel idle capacity plus coordination overhead.
